language.script_notes: Spanish dominates signage, with Quechua and Aymara spoken widely across the highlands and Guaraní in the southeast. The multicoloured checkered Wiphala flag, a symbol of Andean Indigenous peoples, flies widely and is a strong national tell.

road_furniture.bollard_color: Rounded-top posts in varied colours; some lack white reflectors and sit on corners, working like a chevron. Red-and-white bollards appear on some routes.
road_furniture.guardrail_type: Striped guardrails with a yellow outer stripe (Peru's uses a black outer stripe instead).
road_furniture.line_paint: Orange or yellow center lines are common, alongside white edge lines.
road_furniture.curb_style: Cobblestone and large stone paving in some towns; many roads are unpaved dirt.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Utility poles are thick square lumber (sometimes metal) and often curvy; road signs are frequently mounted on thick, unpainted posts. Dolls hung on poles as anti-theft warnings appear in La Paz. YPFB (state oil) diamond-shaped logos are a strong fuel-station tell.

architecture.roof_style: Flat roofs of concrete or corrugated metal; simple pitched roofs on rural buildings.
architecture.roof_material: Corrugated metal and flat concrete, with red clay tile in colonial towns.
architecture.wall_construction: Mostly brick and cement construction, rarely wood; simpler brick buildings at high altitude, cement-painted walls in the lowlands; blue-and-white painted buildings often mark the state telecom (Entel) or a political party; La Paz–El Alto has the flamboyant neo-Andean 'cholet' buildings; Sucre requires whitewashed walls in its historic district.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Unpainted brick and grey cement, with vividly painted cholets and whitewashed colonial walls.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Brightly coloured neo-Andean cholets with event halls topped by a rooftop residence; unfinished brick buildings; whitewashed colonial churches and plazas; adobe villages on the Altiplano.

nature.vegetation: Treeless Altiplano grassland with ichu grass and thola shrubs in the west; cloud forest on the eastern Andean slopes; flat, green, extensively forested and farmed lowlands in the east.
nature.terrain: A landlocked country of extremes — the high Andean plateau (Altiplano) with the world's largest salt flat, volcanic peaks, and steep fog-prone mountain roads in the west, dropping to flat Amazon and Chaco lowlands in the east.
nature.climate_signature: Cold, thin-aired and sunny at altitude; hot and humid in the lowlands — the country's two halves look nothing alike.

vehicles.plate_color: White plates that look faintly blue in Street View.
vehicles.plate_format: Three or four digits followed by three letters (e.g. '1234-ABC').
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Minibuses (micros) and shared taxis are common in La Paz; used Japanese imports dominate; the Street View car has a white back and no antenna.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Mostly Gen 3 with a white-backed car without an antenna.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Concentrated on the main national routes and around La Paz, Cochabamba and Santa Cruz; large gaps in remote parts including Sajama National Park.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared Andean altiplano, Quechua and Aymara culture and striped mountain guardrails
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Peruvian guardrails use a black outer stripe versus a yellow one here; tuktuks and Peru's black-and-white striped sign poles are absent; the country here is landlocked.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared high-Andean plateau, salt flats and volcanoes in the southwest
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Chilean bollards carry yellow reflectors and Argentina uses a black Gen 3 car; thick unpainted lumber poles, cholet buildings and the Wiphala flag are found here.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Shared Chaco lowlands in the southeast, similar flat green farmland
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Paraguayan plates and Guaraní-influenced signage differ; the highlands and their distinctive road furniture are only here.
